title: Deterministic context win 1: send spec, acceptance and scope once per execute prompt (packet only), all three render call sites
spec:
P0 audit finding (docs/context-economy/00-audit.md, plan.md): every execute prompt carries spec, acceptance and scope twice: once inside the packet built by spawn._packet_body (sections objective "- discovery: {spec}", acceptance, write_scope; spawn.py ~286-305) and again as literal lines in .orchestrator/prompts/execute.md ("Spec: {{spec}}", "Acceptance: {{acceptance}}", "Scope (only these paths): {{scope}}"). The P1 telemetry (merged before this task; context field on runs, per-section meta) is the before/after measure.
Do:
1. .orchestrator/prompts/execute.md: remove the three literal lines. Replace with one line: "The packet above is the task contract: implement the ## objective, satisfy every line of ## acceptance, and edit only paths listed in ## write_scope." Keep every other instruction line verbatim (gate loop, commit, unittest rules, _harness rule, dependencies, tool-call budget).
2. spawn.render: execute no longer needs spec/acceptance/scope kwargs. Update the three call sites so they pass only packet= (spawn.py:773-774 run_worker, daemon.py:561 _dispatch_fresh_fix, daemon.py:853 dispatch). render()'s unfilled-placeholder check must still pass (no leftover {{spec}} tokens) and extra kwargs must not be silently required; if any call site appends more text after render (spawn.py:774 `+ \`), keep that text.
3. Packet guarantee: _packet_body must keep objective (with the full spec), acceptance and write_scope untrimmable even when the packet is over the 4800-char cap (they already are: trimmable = dependencies, evidence, decisions, gotchas, symbols, relevant_tests). Add a regression test that a task with a 9000-char spec and 6 acceptance lines still has every acceptance line and the full spec text and every scope path in the rendered execute prompt exactly once.
4. Fix-round path: _dispatch_fresh_fix renders execute for the fix task; the fix task's spec is the fix-round spec (failures + acceptance). Verify the packet's objective carries it and nothing is lost; the repair delta path (executor.reply) is unaffected.
5. Update P1 telemetry expectations if a test in tests/test_spawn.py or tests/test_daemon.py asserts on instruction tokens or on the literal "Spec:" line; adjust the expected numbers, never weaken the assertion shape.
6. Record the measured delta in docs/context-economy/03-dedup-execute-prompt.md (≤30 lines): chars and est_tokens of the execute prompt for one representative task before and after (use spawn.packet_run_meta or the P1 section meta on a fixture task), and the revert path (git revert the commit).
Tests: tests/test_spawn.py::test_execute_prompt_carries_contract_once (spec, each acceptance line and each scope path appear exactly once in the rendered prompt; no "Spec:" literal); tests/test_daemon.py::test_fresh_fix_prompt_renders_without_contract_kwargs (the fresh-fix render path succeeds and the prompt contains the fix spec once). Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result.
acceptance: .orchestrator/prompts/execute.md has no {{spec}}, {{acceptance}} or {{scope}} placeholders and all three render call sites pass only packet=
docs/context-economy/03-dedup-execute-prompt.md records before/after chars and est_tokens; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0
